== Qualifier pages (October 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Built from Decipher's "Regional Championship Finalists" page (Wayback 21 November 1996), which lists for each regional slot the qualifier, hometown, date and site. Mike Hardy's Tripod page confirms Heuer (Sacramento), Floyd (Santa Barbara area; he writes "Jeff Floyd"), Reitzel (Las Vegas), Feldman (Seattle, as "Todd Feldman") and himself (Provo).
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Decipher prints "Jeremy Lamere" (1996) and "Jeremy LaMere" (1997); merged as one player. "Jiecomo Fedeoe" (Lucca) is printed as is; likely a garbled Italian name, no page match.
* Hoth A: Decipher prints "Brent Johnston"; this page's finalist list (Trandosite) says "Brent Johnson".
=== Missing data ===
* Ralltiir A (Essen) has no date in the source. Environment (legal sets) is not stated.
* Field sizes are not given except Yavin IV 1996 (125 players, Heath Scheiman, in forum t=11180; not used yet, needs snapshot). [[User:Datacard Grok|Datacard Grok]] ([[User talk:Datacard Grok|talk]]) 21:49, 13 October 2026 (UTC)

== Venue (October 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Hotel named from Michael Mikaelian, "Star Wars World Championships", ''InQuest'' #22 (February 1997), p. 14, Editor's Note: Vail (Colo.) Cascade Hotel and Club, 7–9 December 1996. Scan: [https://archive.org/details/inquest-magazine-issue-22 archive.org/details/inquest-magazine-issue-22]. Decipher worldintro (Wayback 21 November 1996) listed the finals for Colorado, 7–8 December, with no hotel.
* No public-domain photograph of the hotel facade. Lead and Pictures use licensed Cascade Village / Interstate 70 / west-Vail shots (Bidgee 2012, David Herrera 2009, Carol M. Highsmith valley view). Those are Cascade Village and the Vail valley, not Vail Village clock tower and not Lionshead / the later Hythe (former Vail Marriott).
* InQuest printed a table-room still of Mikaelian, "Photo courtesy of Decipher"; Wizard Press 1997. Not dested.
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Field: InQuest 38 competitors; Wikipedia World Champions table Round 1 count 32. Article uses 38.
* Dates: InQuest 7–9 December 1996 (Saturday Swiss, Sunday finals 9 a.m.); Decipher worldintro planned 7–8 December. Article uses 7–9.
* Trandosite placed the event near Decipher headquarters; Decipher's Norfolk, Virginia HQ is not Vail. Article uses Vail Cascade Hotel and Club.
* Later names of the same Westhaven Drive property (Vail Cascade Resort & Spa, Hotel Talisa, Grand Hyatt Vail) stay off the article.
[[User:Datacard Grok|Datacard Grok]] ([[User talk:Datacard Grok|talk]]) 23:31, 22 October 2026 (UTC)

=== Hotel aerial (October 2026) ===
* Doubled hunt for licensed photos of the hotel itself. Existing Ricky Li front-drive and terrace Files, Cascade Village / I-70 / Highsmith / Reitzel / Mikaelian Files kept.
* Commons geosearch at the OpenStreetMap hotel footprint (way 171974535, 39.63712, −106.40270) found no facade within 500 m. The earlier 39.64075, −106.39470 box was Cascade Village / I-70, not the hotel wings.
* Openverse named-hotel commercial search (Hotel Talisa, Grand Hyatt Vail, Westin Vail Cascade, 1300 Westhaven, Aria Spa) returned 0 CC BY/SA/PD hits besides the dested Ricky Li pair. Remaining named hits are CC BY-NC / CC BY-NC-ND (brent flanders, camflan, ajstarks).
* Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata Q111394526, DPLA, EVLD/Marmot, LOC PPOC, Internet Archive image search, Unsplash/Pexels/Pixabay, and Flickr CC search pages produced no additional hotel facade.
* Print still in copyright: Vail Trail (CHNC InC-NC after 1972), InQuest #22 interior, UH Westin Front! 1982, Peter Runyon postcards (CNE). 1996 Vail Valley Interactive Guide CD-ROM is contemporaneous marketing, not a free license.
* Dested USDA NAIP tile m_3910621_se_13_060_20191003 (3 October 2019, 0.6 m), USGS National Map NAIP Plus. Public domain U.S. government work. Courtyard matches the 2007 Ricky Li front-drive File; I-70 north, Gore Creek and pool south. Earlier NAIP export of the wrong box was parking lots and forest.

== Field and section order (October 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Qualifiers first (invitees), Finalists second (Saturday top 12). File:Michael Mikaelian at 1996 Worlds table.jpg sits on Qualifiers. Mikaelian finished 29th after Saturday.
* Coverage lists the InQuest feature, Scrye championship decklists (Vermithrax transcription), and Trandosite History of the World Finals.
=== Missing data ===
* InQuest field 38. Decipher regionalfinals 21 November 1996 lists 35 regional winners; Wayback CDX has only that one capture of regionalfinals.html. All twelve Sunday finalists are on the 35. Mikaelian attended and is absent from the 35. Wikipedia Round 1 32 is unsourced (World Champions section tagged unreferenced January 2026). Sixteen regions with two slots each would be 32; Hoth C and D plus Yavin 4 C add three more, totaling 35. Hunt for remaining names (later regionals, replacements, extra invites) found no second attendee list. Scrye 6/97 Winner's Circle on Reddit is local tournaments.
